metadata.description: Claude Code plugins for this catalog — agent tooling, the TypeScript and SvelteKit stacks, Rust, interface craft and motion, native Apple apps, Godot games, containers and self-hosted infrastructure (Docker, Unraid, Dokploy), OWASP-grounded security review, OpenSpec workflow setup, the Zed editor, PARA file organization, and Windows apps on a Mac with CrossOver.

plugins.name: meta-skills
plugins.description: Authoring and maintenance skills for Claude Code's own extension surfaces — skills, subagents, hooks, plugins, and the marketplaces that distribute them — plus prompt rewriting, project memory, a repo-root TOOLS.md map, and Controlled Engineering English for documentation. Ships the `controlled-english` output style.

plugins.name: typescript
plugins.description: The TypeScript toolchain end to end — compiler settings and type-level design for new code, tightening loose types and migrating JavaScript incrementally, reading compiler errors that do not say what they mean, testing with Vitest, bundling with Vite, formatting and linting with Biome, typed database schemas and migrations with Drizzle ORM, and running it all on Bun.

plugins.name: frontend
plugins.description: The web application stack this organisation builds on, leaning SvelteKit — headless components with Bits UI, charts with LayerChart, Tailwind CSS v4 themes and utilities, BEM class naming, Feature-Sliced Design layout, internationalization with Paraglide JS and @internationalized/date, and sanitizing untrusted HTML with DOMPurify.

plugins.name: design-engineering
plugins.description: Interface craft and motion on the Svelte stack — building an animation from the decisions that determine whether it feels right, reviewing motion against a strict bar, auditing a codebase's motion into executable plans, finding the places that should animate and rejecting the ones that should not, naming an effect you can only describe, the component-craft philosophy underneath all of it, and Apple's fluid-interface principles for gestures, springs, materials, and type.

plugins.name: docker-workbench
plugins.description: Set up, use, and configure Docker and containers — Dockerfiles and Compose, dev containers for VS Code and Codespaces, runtime setup across OrbStack, Docker Desktop, Colima and Engine, runtime hardening, vulnerability scanning and image signing, isolated build/runtime debugging, and a guard against irreversible volume loss.

plugins.name: security
plugins.description: OWASP-grounded security review. Audits a branch diff or a whole repository against a vendored, pinned copy of the OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, citing a cheatsheet section and a verbatim quote for every finding, checked by a verifier that CI runs over every committed report. Also ships an advisory PostToolUse hook that flags high-confidence credential formats in files Claude writes.

plugins.name: workflows
plugins.description: Sets up or reconciles a project's OpenSpec workflow in one command: schemas and subagents for a chosen complexity level, a rewritten openspec/config.yaml that carries forward what you wrote, and guarded plugin installation. Re-runnable, with --check for read-only drift reporting. Also routes a piece of work to the right schema among the seventeen it installs, detects Apple-native repos and adds the apple-studio layer plus an app-release workflow at the advanced level, and ships a self-paced learning package covering installation, routing, and every workflow end to end.

plugins.name: unraid-ops
plugins.description: Unraid server administration: parity array, pools, shares, Docker, VMs, remote access, performance and failure recovery — with a guard against the documented data-loss command patterns and read-only access to the Unraid GraphQL API.

plugins.name: dokploy
plugins.description: Self-hosted Dokploy PaaS: deploying applications through Nixpacks, Railpack, Dockerfile, Buildpack, and static builds with domains, certificates, and vault-backed environment variables; operating the host — installation, remote and dedicated build servers, cluster, panel and database backups with tested restores, and symptom-first troubleshooting; scripting the full CLI and API surface, which the published documentation covers only in part; hardening the panel, Traefik, and secrets against a 25-control checklist mapped to SOC 2 and ISO 27001; configuring enterprise SSO, SCIM, custom roles, and audit logs; and a guard against irreversible project, database, and volume removal.

plugins.name: zed
plugins.description: Configures and customizes the Zed editor — settings.json and keymap.json, themes and fonts, per-language and LSP options, formatters, tasks, snippets, extensions, and AI and agent configuration.

plugins.name: apple-studio
plugins.description: Native Apple app development for SwiftUI and Swift 6 — architecture and state, strict concurrency, Swift Testing, Human Interface Guidelines conformance and accessibility, adaptive layout across sizes, poses, and foldables, SwiftUI motion, native macOS apps, the first-party framework map, on-device generative AI with Foundation Models, performance diagnosis with Instruments, App Store release engineering, and the build-test-screenshot loop. Ships a build gate that blocks a session ending on a failed build after Swift edits.

plugins.name: para
plugins.description: Organizes a directory into Tiago Forte's PARA structure — Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives — through an approve-before-move workflow: a plan grouped by decision rather than by file, classification from metadata and macOS Spotlight signals with a bounded content peek, a project list you own and correct, and an undo manifest for every move. Ships /para:organize and a guard hook that blocks deletion and unplanned moves inside a managed root.

plugins.name: godot
plugins.description: Game development with Godot 4 — project and scene architecture, the .tscn and .tres file formats and their uid:// identity rules, GDScript with static typing, and a verify loop built on the engine's own headless tooling. Ships a read-only MCP server that parses a project, checks scripts and shaders, runs scenes, captures screenshots, and serves the class reference generated from the user's own engine binary, plus a guard against the file moves that break uid:// references unrepairably.

plugins.name: crossover
plugins.description: Running Windows applications and games on a Mac with CodeWeavers CrossOver — bottles, installing listed and unlisted applications, the command-line tools, registry and Wine Configuration changes, Advanced Settings per CrossOver version (23.7–24, 25, 26), debug logs, locale and keyboard fixes, and controllers, anti-cheat, and mods — built from the CodeWeavers Mac knowledge base. Ships a log-triage agent for .cxlog files and a guard against irreversible bottle deletion.

plugins.name: rust
plugins.description: Rust development on the 2024 edition, built from the official Rust documentation, the Rust API Guidelines, and the Clippy book — the language and the standard library, with the edition-2024 changes and APIs stabilised through Rust 1.99; Cargo manifests, features, workspaces, profiles, build scripts, configuration, cross-compilation, and publishing; designing public APIs against the API Guidelines checklist; Clippy lint policy, clippy.toml, and rustfmt; reading compiler errors and lints; atomics, memory ordering, and building locks and other synchronization primitives, from Mara Bos's Rust Atomics and Locks; testing; rustdoc and doctests; and command-line applications on current crates. Ships a build-triage agent that returns only root-cause diagnostics, an API-review agent that checks a crate's public surface against the guidelines, a Stop gate that keeps a session from ending while cargo check fails after Rust edits, and a guard that asks before cargo publish, yank, and owner changes.
